# AI opportunity and value portfolio - worked example

**UIOWA-072.** Generated by `opportunity_portfolio.py`. Deterministic: no clock, no RNG, sorted traversal.

> EVERY CANDIDATE, NUMBER, GROUP AND MEASURE BELOW IS FICTION, written to exercise the model. None of it is a University of Iowa finding, none of it came from University systems, and none of it should be quoted as an observation about AIS. Real values replace these once University evidence arrives; the basis field on each assumption records which ones are still invented.

## How to read this

Three ledgers are reported separately and are never summed: one-time implementation (hours (one-time)), recurring maintenance (FTE-fraction per year (recurring)), and expected benefit (staff-hours released per year (recurring)). Adding across them raises LedgerUnitError.

- Every figure is a **low - likely - high range**. A single number would state a precision this evidence does not support.
- **UNKNOWN means not assessed.** It is never scored as zero, never averaged away, and never dropped from the table.
- Candidates whose benefit ranges overlap share a rank. They are not separable on current evidence, and presenting them as #2 and #3 would be invented precision.
- Benefit is **screening arithmetic in staff-hours**. No labour rates, no currency, no break-even: that belongs to the AI benefit and operating-cost model (UIOWA-078). Detailed effort build-up belongs to the resource estimator (UIOWA-086).

Declared constants: `2080` hours per FTE-year (used only for a side-by-side context line), effort-heavy line at `1` years payback.

## Candidate detail

### `OPP-IAM-01` - Explain access-request denials in plain language to the requester (IAM)

*When an access request is denied, the requester currently receives an entitlement code. An analyst writes a plain-language explanation on request. The explanation is short and easy to build, but it depends on an entitlement vocabulary that changes continuously as applications are onboarded and roles are restructured.*

- **Decision:** PURSUE - benefit is positive across the whole stated range (37.5 - 138.2 - 274.0 h/yr) with inputs available.
- **Rank note:** TIED - not separable on current evidence (benefit intervals overlap with OPP-RIS-01)
- **Flag:** RECURRING-LOAD-EXCEEDS-BENEFIT: recurring upkeep at the likely case is about 374 h/yr of capacity, against 138 h/yr released. These are separate ledgers and are not netted; read both before treating the 0.40-year payback as the whole story.
- **Dimensions:** task_suitability=HIGH, expected_benefit=ASSESSED, input_availability=HIGH, integration_effort=ASSESSED, measurable_success=HIGH
- **Recurring load in context:** 208 - 374 - 624 h/yr equivalent. context only, at 2080 h/FTE-yr; NOT added to the one-time ledger
- **Outcomes to measure:**
  - Denied requests followed by a clarification contact: denials followed by a contact within 5 days / denials, monthly, baseline 0.41
  - Resubmitted requests that succeed on the next attempt: successful resubmissions / resubmissions after a denial, monthly, baseline 0.53

### `OPP-RIS-01` - Summarise sponsor policy documents into award-setup checklists (RIS)

*Award setup staff read sponsor terms and produce a setup checklist. The reading is genuine language work over long documents, but the policy corpus is scattered across shared drives and a website, with more than one version of the same policy in circulation and no retrieval layer over any of it.*

- **Decision:** PURSUE-BUT-EFFORT-HEAVY - positive benefit (138.0 - 222.9 - 322.6 h/yr) but input availability is LOW: the required inputs have to be assembled before any of it is reachable.
- **Rank note:** TIED - not separable on current evidence (benefit intervals overlap with OPP-IAM-01)
- **Flag:** RECURRING-LOAD-EXCEEDS-BENEFIT: recurring upkeep at the likely case is about 250 h/yr of capacity, against 223 h/yr released. These are separate ledgers and are not netted; read both before treating the 1.88-year payback as the whole story.
- **Dimensions:** task_suitability=HIGH, expected_benefit=ASSESSED, input_availability=LOW, integration_effort=ASSESSED, measurable_success=MODERATE
- **Recurring load in context:** 125 - 250 - 458 h/yr equivalent. context only, at 2080 h/FTE-yr; NOT added to the one-time ledger
- **Outcomes to measure:**
  - Award setups completed within target days of terms receipt: setups within target / setups in the period, monthly, baseline 0.74
  - Checklist items corrected at review: corrected items / checklist items produced, monthly, **baseline required** - not yet measurable, and not recorded as 0
- **Evidence needed from the University:**
  - How often sponsor terms are reissued, which sets the recurring corpus-refresh load.
  - Whether a single authoritative copy of each sponsor policy exists, and who owns it.

### `OPP-ESS-01` - Draft first-pass release notes from merged change records (ESS)

*A delivery lead hand-writes release notes for each student-system release by reading the merged change records. The drafting is language work over records that are already structured and already in one place; a human still edits and approves every note before it is published.*

- **Decision:** PURSUE - benefit is positive across the whole stated range (26.4 - 68.0 - 113.0 h/yr) with inputs available.
- **Dimensions:** task_suitability=HIGH, expected_benefit=ASSESSED, input_availability=HIGH, integration_effort=ASSESSED, measurable_success=HIGH
- **Recurring load in context:** 21 - 42 - 83 h/yr equivalent. context only, at 2080 h/FTE-yr; NOT added to the one-time ledger
- **Outcomes to measure:**
  - Release notes published within one business day of release: releases with notes published within 1 business day / releases in the period, per release, baseline 0.62
  - Editor changes per published note: edited lines / drafted lines, per release, baseline n/a for manual baseline - manual notes are authored, not edited; recorded as the comparison point, not as zero

### `OPP-ESS-02` - Auto-classify inbound registration support tickets to a routing queue (ESS)

*Front-line staff route incoming registration tickets to the right queue. Routing already takes about two minutes, and a misroute during the registration peak costs far more than it saves, so every suggested route is confirmed by a person before it is applied.*

- **Decision:** UNCERTAIN-NET-VALUE - benefit range straddles zero (-1041.7 - -256.7 - 10.4 h/yr): on current assumptions this can lose time as easily as save it.
- **Dimensions:** task_suitability=MODERATE, expected_benefit=ASSESSED, input_availability=HIGH, integration_effort=ASSESSED, measurable_success=MODERATE
- **Recurring load in context:** 62 - 125 - 250 h/yr equivalent. context only, at 2080 h/FTE-yr; NOT added to the one-time ledger
- **Outcomes to measure:**
  - Tickets routed correctly on first assignment: tickets not re-queued / tickets routed, monthly, baseline 0.91
  - Median minutes from ticket arrival to correct queue: minutes to correct queue / tickets routed, monthly, **baseline required** - not yet measurable, and not recorded as 0
- **Evidence needed from the University:**
  - A measured misroute rate and the real downstream cost of a misroute during the registration peak. The whole result turns on this number.

### `OPP-IAM-02` - Draft quarterly access-review summaries for application owners (IAM)

*Application owners certify entitlements each quarter. A drafted summary of what changed since the last review would shorten the certification. Whether the prior review records are retrievable in a usable form is not currently known to anyone we could ask, so the size of the task is not known either.*

- **Decision:** BLOCKED-UNKNOWN - cannot be ranked: expected_benefit, input_availability not assessed. Absent evidence is held as UNKNOWN, not scored as zero.
- **Rank note:** UNRANKED - pending expected_benefit, input_availability
- **Dimensions:** task_suitability=HIGH, expected_benefit=UNKNOWN, input_availability=UNKNOWN, integration_effort=ASSESSED, measurable_success=MODERATE
- **Recurring load in context:** 83 - 166 - 312 h/yr equivalent. context only, at 2080 h/FTE-yr; NOT added to the one-time ledger
- **Outcomes to measure:**
  - Access reviews certified by the quarter deadline: reviews certified on time / reviews due, quarterly, **baseline required** - not yet measurable, and not recorded as 0
- **Evidence needed from the University:**
  - Are prior quarterly access-review records retained, and can two consecutive quarters be compared?
  - How many application owners certify each quarter, and how long does a certification take today?

### `OPP-RIS-02` - Generate effort-certification reminder narratives (RIS)

*Certifiers receive a reminder naming the periods and projects awaiting certification. The content is entirely determined by fields already in the record; the reminder is a fill-in, not a composition. A deterministic template already does this correctly and needs no checking.*

- **Decision:** DO-NOT-PURSUE - task suitability is LOW: the work is not language-shaped, so an assisted workflow adds a checking step without removing one. The arithmetic agrees independently: even the optimistic bound releases no staff time (-346.0 - -122.2 - -11.0 h/yr).
- **Rank note:** UNRANKED - DO-NOT-PURSUE
- **Dimensions:** task_suitability=LOW, expected_benefit=ASSESSED, input_availability=HIGH, integration_effort=ASSESSED, measurable_success=HIGH
- **Recurring load in context:** 42 - 83 - 166 h/yr equivalent. context only, at 2080 h/FTE-yr; NOT added to the one-time ledger
- **Outcomes to measure:**
  - Certifications completed by the period deadline: certifications on time / certifications due, per certification period, baseline 0.88

## Which assumptions the ranking actually stands on

These assumptions change a rank or a decision class when swung to their own stated bounds. Collect evidence for these first; the rest can move freely without changing the answer.

| Candidate | Assumption | Basis | What changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPP-ESS-01` | one_time_implementation_hours | ASSUMED | high bound -> rank 3, class PURSUE-BUT-EFFORT-HEAVY |
| `OPP-ESS-02` | assisted_minutes_per_item | ASSUMED | high bound -> unranked, class DO-NOT-PURSUE |
| `OPP-ESS-02` | baseline_minutes_per_item | ASSUMED | low bound -> unranked, class DO-NOT-PURSUE |
| `OPP-ESS-02` | checking_minutes_per_item | ASSUMED | high bound -> unranked, class DO-NOT-PURSUE |
| `OPP-ESS-02` | repair_minutes_per_reworked_item | ASSUMED | high bound -> unranked, class DO-NOT-PURSUE |
| `OPP-ESS-02` | rework_rate | ASSUMED | high bound -> unranked, class DO-NOT-PURSUE |
| `OPP-IAM-01` | baseline_minutes_per_item | ASSUMED | low bound -> rank 2, class PURSUE |
